insight.headline: The offense hasn't matched the pitching.
insight.detail: The staff is holding at 3.96 ERA, but a .654 OPS at the plate has made it difficult. San Francisco sits at 6-4 over their last ten with neither side pulling ahead.
insight.why: ERA at 3.96 · quiet bats (.654 OPS) · 6–4 in the last ten

narrative.top_frame: Down six with one out left, they didn't find it.
narrative.what_this_means: A 0-0 scoreboard is not an excuse. It's a verdict. They had chances—Webb was sharp, but so was Philadelphia's rotation. The real problem: they couldn't generate anything when it mattered. No rallies. No traffic with runners in scoring position. Just empty swings in the moments that decided the game. This is what inconsistency looks like when the margin disappears. They beat themselves before the other team beat them. A .245 average doesn't win tight games, and this team keeps finding tight games. The pattern has become unavoidable.
narrative.what_to_watch: Now the question is whether Webb's favorable matchup against Philadelphia's struggling lineup (.223) lets them reset the formula, or whether the damage from last night—a night they should have stolen—starts to compound.
